candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity: use therapeutic communication; assess coping, self-concept, mood and psychosocial responses to health alterations; provide support and coordinate referrals/resources when indicated.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Therapeutic communication, coping assessment, and individualized psychosocial support after major body change
candidate.educational_objective: Use therapeutic communication after limb loss to assess individualized body-image concerns, mood, coping and social participation and connect the client with preferred psychosocial resources without minimizing or universalizing the adjustment process.

options.A: Explore the client's feelings and goals without assuming everyone responds the same way, assess mood, coping and social withdrawal, and offer individualized resources such as a psychologist, social worker, or peer counselor if the client wants or needs additional support.
options.B: Tell the client that appearance should not matter and redirect the conversation to prosthetic training so negative feelings are not reinforced.
options.C: Require attendance at a peer-support group because every person with an amputation needs the same psychosocial intervention to adjust successfully.
options.D: Avoid discussing body image or social withdrawal because psychological adjustment is separate from rehabilitation and does not affect quality of life or participation.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current VA/DoD amputation-rehabilitation guidance treats psychosocial limitations and quality of life as integral parts of rehabilitation, not separate from physical recovery. VA patient guidance recognizes that limb loss can produce varied emotional responses and recommends listening to the individual's needs; a psychologist, social worker, or peer counselor can provide additional support when appropriate. B minimizes the client's expressed concern and shuts down therapeutic communication. C is overly prescriptive because support needs and preferences vary; peer support is a resource, not a mandatory intervention for every client. D incorrectly separates psychosocial recovery from rehabilitation. The final item therefore tests individualized assessment and support rather than assuming a uniform body-image response after amputation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current VA/DoD and VA patient resources directly support individualized psychosocial assessment after limb loss and optional referral to psychology, social work or peer support according to the client's needs and preferences.
